originalTitle: Morning Mail: inside the political ‘meme factories’; China questions detainee’s death; Netanyahu rejects Trump’s Gaza plan
summary: ‘Buzzer’ economy drumming up outrage online; China’s ‘grave concern’ over death in detention; Trump’s Gaza peace plan in doubt
content: Good morning. Today we speak to a member of a “meme factory” in Indonesia who is busy trading outrage about Australian politics online as Facebook’s owner, Meta, pays for her efforts. Another exclusive story reveals that Chinese officials have raised serious questions about whether a Chinese citizen was properly monitored before she died in a Melbourne detention centre run by a US prison giant. With house auctions on shaky ground across Australia, we ask whether we still need this weekend ritual. And Benjamin Netanyahu has cast further doubt over Middle East peace efforts by rejecting Donald Trump’s Gaza plan. Australia Exclusive | Chinese officials have expressed “grave concern” as documents reveal a suicide warning before a woman’s death in a Melbourne immigration detention centre run by a US private firm. Cash for clicks | Workers in Indonesia’s “buzzer” economy are propagating outrage on social media – including about Pauline Hanson’s One Nation party – not for any political motive, but because Meta pays for engagement. Clearing out | Recent falls in auction clearance rates are resulting in dramatic headlines featuring words like “horror”, “failure” and “wipe out”. Is Australia’s love affair with auctions coming to an end? The Agenda | As the spring parliamentary session begins, Labor’s gambling reforms face pressure from all sides. Will they hold ’em, fold ’em or walk away? Body discovered | The body of a woman was found in a suitcase by the side of a road at Oallen, south of Goulburn, in regional New South Wales. World Middle East crisis | Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has rejected a US-backed peace plan for Gaza in a rare public break with Donald Trump; Iran-aligned Houthis claim they have attacked an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. Wildfire threats | Canada’s government will provide urgent assistance to British Columbia after an onslaught of unprecedented fast-moving wildfires forced about 22,000 people to flee their homes. Ceuta fallout | Italy has condemned Spain’s “incomprehensible” border controls as people making their way between the two EU countries grapple with the effects of their escalating feud. Typhoon Dolphin | The most powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year has made landfall on the country’s east coast, bringing torrential rain and warnings of flooding and landslides. ‘You’re hit with a slam of shadow’ | Two Nasa aviators are set to take off from Iceland on a mission to photograph the sun by flying at 740km/h along the path of a solar eclipse. Full Story Why hasn’t Labor had another female leader? Tanya Plibersek has got the profile and a long list of credentials. But in the conversation of who is in line to be Labor’s next leader after Anthony Albanese, she barely registers, and nor do any other women. And that’s despite the party achieving gender parity in its caucus. Krishani Dhanji speaks with Rafqa Touma about why it’s been a long time since a woman led the Labor party. In-depth Australia has often sought to reassure itself that at least the nation is untainted, unlike Britain and the US, by a heinous history of slavery. But a new book traces how Sydney’s sugar rush profited from the capture and sale of “blackbirded” Pacific Islanders. The work highlights how the evidence of blackbirding is hiding in plain sight, with its legacies only now being grappled with. Not the news Within the first 10 minutes of My Brilliant Career, Netflix’s new take on the classic Australian novel by Miles Franklin, there’s smutty performance poetry and a Divinyls needle drop that suggests it’s not going to be your standard turn-of-the-century period drama. “It’s bonkers,” admits Philippa Northeast, who plays our wild, passionate and indomitable teen heroine Sybylla Melvin. Sport Cycling | Demi Vollering held off Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney in a dramatic final stage victory to win the Tour de France Femmes in Nice. AFL | The Demons stunned the Dockers in an extraordinary thriller to emerge as a bona fide premiership threat, Brendan Foster writes; AFLW’s good old familiarity hit the big stage in a women’s and men’s double-header. Football | La Liga’s president, Javier Tebas, says the “Gianni Infantino era is over” at Fifa; versatile Bruno Guimarães gives Mikel Arteta options to shuffle Arsenal’s midfield pack, Ed Aarons writes; Andoni Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as frailties in defence prove costly. Tennis | “I’m not ready to compete”: Jannik Sinner has pulled out of this week’s Cincinnati Open. Media roundup There are warnings that more than 15.5 million Australians will have no say in who inherits their superannuation, ABC News reports. To combat the threat of AI, a radical overhaul of the HSC would bar year 12 students in NSW from completing unsupervised take-home assignments, the Sydney Morning Herald reports. A 3D-printed medical device is offering new hope to Australian women suffering complications from silicone breast implants, the Age reports. What’s happening today NSW | A hearing is being held in Sydney today in the independent “public inquiry” into the Aukus security partnership. NSW | Public hearings in the royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion are due to continue today in Sydney. Sign up If you would like to receive this Morning Mail update to your email inbox every weekday, sign up here, or finish your day with our Afternoon Update newsletter. You can follow the latest in US politics by signing up for This Week in Trumpland. Brain teaser And finally, here are the Guardian’s crosswords to keep you entertained throughout the day. chineseTitle: 早间邮报：政治“模因工厂”内部；中国对被拘留者的死亡提出质疑；内塔尼亚胡拒绝特朗普的加沙计划
chineseSummary: “蜂鸣器”经济在网上引发愤怒；中国对拘留期间死亡表示“严重关切”；特朗普的加沙和平计划受到质疑
chineseContent: 早上好。今天，我们采访了印度尼西亚一家“模因工厂”的一名成员，她正忙着在网上表达对澳大利亚政治的愤怒，Facebook 的所有者 Meta 为她的努力付出了代价。另一篇独家报道透露，中国官员对一名中国公民在美国监狱巨头管理的墨尔本拘留中心死亡前是否受到适当监控提出了严重质疑。由于澳大利亚各地的房屋拍卖都不稳定，我们不禁要问，我们是否还需要这个周末仪式。本杰明·内塔尼亚胡拒绝唐纳德·特朗普的加沙计划，进一步对中东和平努力产生了怀疑。澳洲独家|中国官员表示“严重关切”，因为文件显示一名妇女在一家美国私人公司经营的墨尔本移民拘留中心死亡前曾发出自杀警告。点击现金 |印度尼西亚“蜂鸣器”经济中的工人在社交媒体上散布愤怒情绪，包括对宝琳·汉森 (Pauline Hanson) 的一国党 (One Nation party) 的不满，这并不是出于任何政治动机，而是因为 Meta 为参与付费。清仓|最近拍卖清空率的下降导致出现了一些引人注目的头条新闻，其中包括“恐怖”、“失败”和“消灭”等词语。澳大利亚对拍卖的热爱即将结束吗？议程|随着春季议会会议的开始，工党的赌博改革面临着来自各方的压力。他们会握住它们、折叠它们还是走开？尸体被发现|在新南威尔士州古尔本以南的奥伦的路边，人们在一个手提箱中发现了一具女性尸体。世界中东危机|以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡罕见地公开与唐纳德·特朗普决裂，拒绝了美国支持的加沙和平计划；与伊朗结盟的胡塞武装声称他们袭击了沙特阿拉伯的一家炼油厂。野火威胁
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
